content: 1. The book City Planning: Principles and Best Practices was published in Montreal by the Convention on Biological Diversity. 2. Hunter D, Burlingame B, Remans R, Borelli T, Cogill B, Coradin L, and others contributed to the chapter Biodiversity and Nutrition in the book Connecting Global Priorities: Biodiversity and Human Health, edited by Romanelli C, Cooper D, Campbell-Lendrum D, Mairo M, Karesh WB, and Hunter D. This book was published in Geneva and Montreal by the World Health Organization and the Secretariat of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity in 2015. 3. Hallmann CA, Sorg M, Jongejans E, Siepel H, Hofland N, Schwan H, and others reported a decline of over 75% in total flying insect biomass over 27 years in protected areas. This study was published in PLoS ONE in 2017, volume 12, issue 10, article e0185809. 4. The report Food Environments: Where People Meet the Food System was edited by Campeau C, Coitinho Delmué DC, and Oenema S, and published as Nutrition Report No. 44 in Rome by the United Nations System Standing Committee on Nutrition in 2019. 5. The publication The Traditional Knowledge Advantage was released in Rome by the International Fund for Agricultural Development in 2016. 6. Ali NS and Trivedi C reviewed scientific activities related to botanic gardens and climate change at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Their findings were published in Biodiversity Conservation in 2011, volume 20, issue 2, pages 295–307. 7. Alves RRN and Rosa IML explored the intersection of biodiversity, traditional medicine, and public health in their article published in the Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine in 2007, volume 3, article 14. 8. Golden CD, Rasolofoniaina BJR, Anjaranirina EJG, Nicolas L, Ravaoliny L, and Kremen C highlighted the value of Madagascar's rainforest pharmacopoeia for local and global uses. Their study was published in PLoS ONE in 2012, volume 7, issue 7, article e41221. 9. Unnikrishnan PM and Suneetha MS discussed the linkages between biodiversity, traditional knowledge, and community health in their publication from the United Nations University-Institute of Advanced Studies in Yokohama in 2012. 10. Sheng-Ji P shared ethnobotanical approaches to traditional medicine studies, with experiences from Asia, in Pharmaceutical Biology in 2011, volume 39, supplement 1, pages 74–9. 11. Hamilton AC examined the role of medicinal plants in conservation and livelihoods in his article published in Biodiversity and Conservation in 2004, volume 13, pages 1477–1517. 12. Nijar GS analyzed the Nagoya Protocol on access and benefit-sharing of genetic resources, providing implementation options for developing countries. This analysis was published in Geneva by the South Centre/Centre of Excellence for Biodiversity Law in 2011. 13. Willis KJ authored State of the World’s Plants, published in London by the Royal Botanic Gardens in 2017. 14. The World Health Organization released the Global Report on Traditional and Complementary Medicine 2019 in Geneva in 2019. 15. Roe D, Mulliken T, Milledge S, Mremi J, and Mosha S authored Making a Living or Making a Killing, published in Stevenage by TRAFFIC/International Institute for Environment and Development in 2002. 16. The World Health Organization published the Traditional Medicine Strategy 2014–2023 in Geneva in 2013. 17. Ji H, Shengji P, and Chunlin L conducted an ethnobotanical study on medicinal plants used by the Lisu People in Nujiang, Northwest Yunnan, China. Their findings were published in Economic Botany in 2004, volume 58, supplement 1, pages S253–64. 18. Heywood VH discussed the integration of ethnopharmacology, food production, nutrition, and biodiversity conservation for indigenous peoples in the Journal of Ethnopharmacology in 2011, volume 137, issue 1, pages 1–15. 19. Waylen K explored the use of botanic gardens to improve well-being in a publication by Botanic Gardens Conservation International in Richmond in 2006. 20. Ochola B and Swallow SA examined the links between agriculture and health in a report by the International Food Policy Research Institute in 2006. 21. The Pan American Health Organization published Health in the Americas, 2017 Edition in 2017. 22. The Global Biodiversity Outlook 3 was published in Montreal by the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity in 2010. 23. JC, Oxenford HA, van Tussenbroek BI, Jordan-Dahlgren E, Croquer A, Bastidas C, and others reviewed the CARICOMP Network of Caribbean Marine Laboratories (1985–2007) in Frontiers in Marine Science in January 2019. 24. Wilson R analyzed the impacts of climate change on mangrove ecosystems in Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS) in the Caribbean Marine Climate Change Report Card: Science Review in 2017, pages 61–82. 25. Ahmed N, Thompson S, and Glaser M discussed integrated mangrove-shrimp cultivation and its potential for blue carbon sequestration in AMBIO in 2018, volume 47, issue 4, pages 441–52. 26. Mbow C, Rosenzweig C, Barioni LG, Benton TG, Herrero M, Krishnapillai M, and others contributed to the chapter on food security in the IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Land, published in Geneva by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change in 2019. 27. Tirado MC, Cohen MJ, Aberman N, Meerman J, and Thompson B addressed the challenges of climate change and biofuel production for food and nutrition security in Food Research International in 2010, volume 43, issue 7, pages 1729–44. 28. Field CB, Barros VR, Mastrandrea MD, Mach KJ, Abdrabo MAK, Adger N, and others contributed to the Working Group II report on climate change impacts, adaptation, and vulnerability for the Fifth Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, published by Cambridge University Press in 2014. 29. Sena A authored Land Under Pressure – Health Under Stress, published in Bonn by the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in 2019. 30. The Global Risks Report 2019 (14th Edition) was published in Geneva by the World Economic Forum in 2019. 31. Griscom BW, Adams J, Ellis PW, Houghton RA, Lomax G, Miteva DA, and others proposed natural climate solutions in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2017, volume 114, issue 44, pages 11645–50. 32. Thompson ID provided an overview of the science-policy interface among climate change, biodiversity, and terrestrial land use in the Journal of Forest Research in 2015, volume 20, issue 5, pages 423–9. 33. Vermeulen SJ, Campbell BM, and Ingram JSI examined the relationship between climate change and food systems in Annual Reviews in 2012, volume 37, issue 1, pages 195–222. 34. McMichael AJ, Woodruff RE, and Hales S discussed the present and future risks of climate change on human health in The Lancet in 2006, volume 367, issue 9513, pages 859–69. 35. Battilani P, Toscano P, Van der Fels-Klerx HJ, Moretti A, Leggieri MC, Brera C, and others reported on the increase in aflatoxin B1 contamination in maize in Europe due to climate change in Scientific Reports in 2016, volume 6, article 24328. 36. Kumar P, Mahato DK, Kamle M, Mohanta TK, and Kang SG reviewed aflatoxins as a global concern for food safety and human health in Frontiers in Microbiology in 2017, volume 7, article 468. 37. The World Health Organization launched a special initiative on climate change and health in Small Island Developing States in Geneva in 2018. 38. Tirado MC, Clarke R, Jaykus LA, McQuatters-Gollop A, and Frank JM reviewed the impact of climate change on food safety in Food Research International in 2010, volume 43, issue 7, pages 1745–65. 39. The COP24 Special Report on Health and Climate Change was published in Geneva by the World Health Organization in 2018. 40. Paterson RRM and Lima N explored the effects of climate change on mycotoxins in food in Food Research International in 2010, volume 43, issue 7, pages 1902–14. 41. Patriarca A and Fernández Pinto V reviewed the prevalence of mycotoxins in foods and decontamination methods in Current Opinion in Food Science in 2017, volume 14, pages 50–60. 42. Reddy K, Salleh B, Saad B, Abbas HK, Abel CA, and Shier WT provided an overview of mycotoxin contamination in foods and its implications for human health in Toxin Reviews in 2010, volume 29, issue 1, pages 3–26. 43. Fischer CG and Garnett T authored Plates, Pyramids, Planet, published in Rome by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 2016. 44. McMichael AJ discussed the effects of globalization and climate change on human health in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2013, volume 368, issue 14, pages 1335–43. 45. Smith MR and Myers SS examined the impact of anthropogenic CO2 emissions on global human nutrition in Nature Climate Change in 2018, volume 8, issue 9, pages 834–9. 46. Alae-Carew C, Nicoleau S, Bird FA, Hawkins P, Tuomisto HL, Haines A, and others systematically reviewed the impact of environmental changes on the yield and nutritional quality of fruits, nuts, and seeds in Environmental Research Letters in 2020, volume 15, issue 2, article 023002. 47. Seddon N, Chausson A, Berry P, Girardin CAJ, Smith A, and Turner B discussed the value and limitations of nature-based solutions to climate change and other global challenges in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London B: Biological Sciences in 2020, volume 375, issue 1794, article 20190120. 48. Calliari E, Staccione A, and Mysiak J proposed an assessment framework for climate-proof nature-based solutions in Science of the Total Environment in 2019, volume 656, pages 691–700. 49. Seddon N, Turner B, Berry P, Chausson A, and Girardin CAJ emphasized grounding nature-based climate solutions in sound biodiversity science in Nature Climate Change in 2019, volume 9, issue 2, pages 84–7. 50. Reid H, Bourne A, Muller H, Podvin K, Scorgie S, and Orindi VA developed a framework for assessing the effectiveness of ecosystem-based approaches to adaptation in Resilience in 2018, pages 207–16. 51. Cohen-Shacham E, Walters G, Janzen C, and Maginnis S edited Nature-Based Solutions to Address Global Societal Challenges, published in Gland by the International Union for Conservation of Nature in 2016. 52. Schmidt-Traub G, Obersteiner M, and Mosnier A proposed three steps to fix the broken food system in Nature in 2019, volume 569, issue 7755, pages 181–3. 53. Van den Bosch M and Sang ÅO systematically reviewed urban natural environments as nature-based solutions for improved public health in Environmental Research in 2017, volume 158, pages 373–84. 54. The European Commission published Towards an EU Research and Innovation Policy Agenda for Nature-Based Solutions & Re-Naturing Cities in Luxembourg in 2015. 55. Sall I and Durin G described the daily struggle for integrated community-based protection of West Africa’s marine and coastal ecosystems in Field Actions Science Reports, Special Issue 7, in 2013. 56. Cormier-Salem MC and Panfili J examined mangrove reforestation in Senegal, questioning whether it represents greening or grabbing of coastal zones and deltas, in the African Journal of Aquatic Science in 2016, volume 41, issue 1, pages 89–98. 57. Weiler AM, Hergesheimer C, Brisbois B, Wittman H, Yassi A, and Spiegel JM conducted a meta-narrative mapping exercise on food sovereignty, food security, and health equity in Health Policy Plan in 2015, volume 30, issue 8, pages 1078–92. 58. The Panorama de la Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional en América Latina y el Caribe 2018 was published in Santiago by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, World Food Programme, Pan American Health Organization, and World Health Organization in 2018. 59. Fanzo J, Hawkes C, Udomkesmalee E, Afshin A, Allemandi L, Assery O, and others authored the 2018 Global Nutrition Report, published in Bristol by Development Initiatives in 2018. 60. The World Health Organization published a technical series on adapting to climate-sensitive health impacts, focusing on undernutrition, in Geneva in 2019. 61. The publication Strengthening Nutrition Action was released in Rome by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the World Health Organization in 2018. 62. The World Health Organization published Protecting Health from Climate Change: Vulnerability and Adaptation Assessment in Geneva in 2013. 63. The Health in All Policies: Training Manual was published in Geneva by the World Health Organization in 2015. 64. The publication Progressing the Sustainable Development Goals through Health in All Policies: Case Studies from Around the World was released in Adelaide by the Government of South Australia in 2017. 65. The World Health Organization published Key Learning on Health in All Policies Implementation from Around the World: Information Brochure in Geneva in 2018. 66. Queenan K, Garnier J, Rosenbaum Nielsen L, Buttigieg S, De Meneghi D, Holmberg M, and others outlined a roadmap to a One Health agenda for 2030 in Perspectives in Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Nutrition, and Natural Resources in 2017, volume 12, article 014. 67. Walton M edited One Planet, One Health, published in Sydney by Sydney University Press in 2019. 68. The World Resources Institute published Creating a Sustainable Food Future in 2018. 69. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations published Future Smart Food in Bangkok in 2018. 70. The Global Action Programme on Food Security and Nutrition in Small Island Developing States was published in Rome by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the Office of the High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries, and Small Island Developing States, and the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs in 2017. 71. Tandon N explored opportunities for advancing women’s sustainable and green livelihoods, food security, and small-scale women farmers in Caribbean SIDS in a publication by the International Policy Centre for Inclusive Growth in Brasilia in 2013. 72. Burlingame B and Dernini S edited Sustainable Diets and Biodiversity, published in Rome by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 2012. 73. Cole DC, Sherwood S, Paredes M, Sanin LH, Crissman C, Espinosa P, and others studied the reduction of pesticide exposure and associated neurotoxic burden in an Ecuadorian small farm population in the International Journal of Occupational and Environmental Health in 2007, volume 13, issue 3, pages 281–9. 74. Orozco FA, Cole DC, Ibrahim S, and Wanigaratne S evaluated health promotion outcomes associated with a community-based program to reduce pesticide-related risks among small farm households in Health Promotion International in December 2011, volume 26, issue 4, pages 432–46. 75. Charron DF authored Ecohealth Research in Practice, published in Ottawa by the International Development Research Centre in 2012. 76. Bjørling-Poulsen M, Andersen HR, and Grandjean P examined the potential developmental neurotoxicity of pesticides used in Europe in Environmental Health in 2008, volume 7, article 1. 77. The Joint FAO/WHO Expert Consultation on the Risks and Benefits of Fish Consumption published its report in Rome in 2011. 78. Grandjean P and Landrigan PJ discussed the developmental neurotoxicity of industrial chemicals in The Lancet in 2006, volume 368, issue 9553, pages 2167–78. 79. Ford AES, Graham H, and White PCL integrated human and ecosystem health through ecosystem services frameworks in Ecohealth in 2015, volume 12, issue 4, pages 660–71. 80. Soto D, White P, Dempster T, De Silva S, Flores A, Karakassis Y, and others addressed aquaculture-fisheries interactions through the ecosystem approach to aquaculture (EAA) in the proceedings of the Global Conference on Aquaculture (2010) in Phuket, Thailand, published in Rome by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 2012. 81. The UN Secretary-General published The Future is Now in New York in 2019. 82. The Global Action Programme on Food Security and Nutrition in Small Island Developing States was published in Rome by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 2017. 83. The Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity published Guidance on Integrating Biodiversity Considerations into One Health Approaches in Montreal in 2017. 84. Zimmerer KS and de Haan S discussed agrobiodiversity and a sustainable food future in Nature Plants.
